sections.title: Installation Process
sections.content:
The installation of VenvHub Pro is designed to be as customizable to your needs as possible. After downloading and running the installer, the wizard will guide you through the following steps:

  1. Language selection and version check: Right at the start, you choose the installer language. The program also automatically checks the system and prevents the installation of an older version over a newer one (anti-downgrade protection).
  2. Mode selection / Update detection: The installer intelligently recognizes the state of your system:
    • New installation: You choose between Standard installation for all users (installed in Program Files) and Portable version (everything in a single folder, e.g., on a USB drive).
    • Update: If the application is already installed, the installer automatically offers the option to Update existing installation.
  3. License terms: Reviewing and agreeing to the license terms (AGPLv3) in the selected language.
  4. Folder selection and completion: During a new installation, you choose the destination location. During an update, the folder selection step is automatically skipped (the original path is used). The installer then cleans up old system files (the _internal folder), extracts the new data, automatically configures access permissions for the shared ProgramData folder, and creates shortcuts.

sections.title: What is the difference between Classic and Portable versions?
sections.content:
VenvHub Pro features intelligent environment detection. The way the application stores your settings, downloaded themes (skins), and other data depends entirely on the type of installation you chose.

🏢 Classic Windows Installation

This mode is ideal for regular users who work on a single computer. The application is installed standardly (for example, to C:\Program Files\VenvHubPro) and creates a shortcut in the Start menu.

  • Security: Since Windows protects the Program Files folder against unauthorized writes, the application does not store your personal data there.
  • User separation: If multiple users share one computer (having different Windows accounts), each user will have their own settings and themes.

🧳 Portable Installation

This mode is designed for developers who want an 'all-in-one' application. During this installation, a special _is_portable.ini file is created in the application folder, serving as a marker for portable mode.

  • Independence: The application leaves almost no traces in the Windows system (no registry writes).
  • Mobility: You can copy the entire VenvHub Pro folder to a USB drive and use it outside of your primary drive.

sections.title: Where is my data stored? (Complete Overview)
sections.content:
Depending on the choice above, the application stores its files in different locations on the disk:

Data TypeClassic InstallationPortable Version
Configuration & Themes
(venv_hub_pro_config.json, themes/)		%APPDATA%\VenvHubPro\Directly in the application folder
Local Python Versions
(PyRuntimes/)		C:\ProgramData\VenvHubPro\PyRuntimes
(if not available, %LOCALAPPDATA%\VenvHubPro\PyRuntimes)		Directly in the application folder
Autostart Groups
(autostart_multi/)		%APPDATA%\VenvHubPro\autostart_multi\In the assets/autostart_multi/ folder
Temporary Files
(Downloaded Python ZIPs, etc.)		%APPDATA%\VenvHubPro\Downloads\In the Downloads/ folder

sections.title: Project Transfer, Protection, and Repair Mechanisms
sections.content:
VenvHub Pro includes intelligent protection and repair mechanisms that prevent environment corruption when transferring between different computers or when changing the USB drive letter.

Scenario A: Drive Letter Repair (Embed venvs only)

This mechanism activates automatically at application startup if running in Portable mode (e.g., from a USB drive). Imagine having your USB connected as drive E: at home and as F: at work.

  1. Upon launch, the application detects that it is running from drive F:.
  2. It loads the paths to your portable (Embed) venvs, which still point to drive E:.
  3. It automatically and silently in the background updates all old drive letters to the new letter F:. It repairs not only its own settings, but also the paths inside activation scripts (e.g., activate.bat) of each portable environment.
System Venvs are protected: For system environments, paths to Python (which point to the system drive C:) are never overwritten or modified. They remain in their original state so that they are instantly unlocked when you return to your home computer.

Scenario B: Hardware Lock and Blocking (System Venvs)

This scenario occurs when you transfer a USB drive with system environments (which utilize standard Python installed on your system drive C:) to another computer (PC2), where this Python is missing or has a different version.

  1. When creating a system venv in Portable mode, the program instantly reads your computer's hardware fingerprint (composed of the PC name and the unique ComputerHardwareId identifier from the registry) and writes it to the portable_system_py.json file.
  2. If you connect the USB drive to another computer (PC2), VenvHub Pro immediately detects a hardware mismatch against the portable_system_py.json file.
  3. For security and stability reasons (protection against C-library incompatibilities and corrupted paths), the application completely locks launch (Play), cloning, editing in VS Code, and access to the Pip manager for this venv.
Notice: A locked system venv is neither destroyed nor modified. When reconnecting the USB drive to your original computer (PC1), the program verifies the hardware match and instantly unlocks the venv safely. On a secondary computer (PC2), you can only delete it or create a new clean portable (Embed) venv.

sections.title: First Launch (Configuring Paths)
sections.content:
After a successful installation, launch the application. On the very first run, both the table and the project list will be empty. For the application to function properly, you need to show it where your data is located on the disk.

Open the main Manager window (by clicking the monitor icon button 🖥 in the Minibar -> Settings tab) and in the Basic Paths section, configure the following:

1. Required Paths (Critical for program operation)

  1. Projects Root:
    Click the folder icon 📁 and select the main directory where all your Python projects are stored (for example, D:\Python_Projects). The application will load all subfolders and treat them as individual projects.

  2. Venv Hub:
    This is the location where VenvHub Pro will physically create all virtual environments. We recommend creating a completely empty and dedicated folder solely for this purpose (for example, C:\Venvs or D:\My_Venvs).

2. Optional Paths and Settings (For advanced features)

  1. Local Packages (VenvHub Linker):
    If you develop your own libraries that you want to share across projects without complex installation steps, specify the folder where you store them. Later, you will be able to link them into any Venv with a single click.

  2. Local Packages (pip -e):
    Storage location for packages installed in editable (development) mode via the standard pip install -e.

  3. Root Folder for VS Code Profiles:
    If you want to use isolated (portable) settings and extensions for the VS Code editor, specify the folder where these user profiles should be stored.

  4. Package Manager (Installation Speed):
    At the bottom of the settings, you will find the installer selection. By default, the application uses the classic and stable Pip. If you want to extremely accelerate installation and dependency resolution, switch this option to modern Ultra-fast (UV - Astral).
Single Instance Only: The application is designed to run only one instance at a time. If you attempt to launch it a second time, the currently running window will be brought to the foreground instead.
Practical Notice: Never set 'Venv Hub' directly to your projects directory! The application manages environments centrally (in one place) and connects them to projects only logically. Mixing project code and virtual environments would cause chaos.
